chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said:

I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The human being, when he saves the foodstuff for his year, his back is lightened and he rests, and Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) did not buy a tie (of marriage) until they had secured the foodstuff for their year.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of saving food for the year according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the virtue of food security (it'am al-sanah) as a means to alleviate physical burden and mental anxiety, a practice deeply rooted in the prophetic tradition of preparedness. It specifically highlights the practical wisdom of the Imams, particularly Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah, who prioritized securing their sustenance provisions before finalizing marriage contracts, illustrating the balance between spiritual devotion and worldly responsibility in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,

‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The human being, when he saves the foodstuff for his (whole) year (expenditure), his back is lightened and he would be at rest, and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> were not buying their ties (of marriage) until they<sup>asws</sup> had saved foodstuffs for their<sup>asws</sup> year’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “I heard al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one saves food for one year, his burden becomes light and he feels comfortable.
Abu Ja’far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, would not buy anything before reserving their food for one year.”
